subject: maths
title: Primary 3 Angles: Right Angles and Comparing Angles
seo_title: P3 Angles and Right Angles Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Concepts of angle; right angles; angles greater than or smaller than a right angle
meta_desc: Free P3 maths practice on angles: arms and vertex, right angles, greater or smaller than a right angle, counting angles and turns. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: An angle is two straight arms meeting at a vertex. Its size is how wide the arms open.
key_sub: At 3 o’clock the clock hands make a right angle; at 1 o’clock the angle is smaller than a right angle.
body_html:
What is an angle?

An angle is made when two straight lines meet at a point. The two lines are the arms. The point where they meet is the vertex.

Right angles

A right angle is a square corner. A small square in a corner shows a right angle. Make a right-angle checker: fold a piece of paper in half, then in half again.

Greater or smaller than a right angle

Put your checker in the angle. If the angle is narrower, it is smaller than a right angle. If it is wider, it is greater than a right angle.

Example

At 5 o’clock, what angle do the hands of a clock make?

At 3 o’clock the hands make a right angle (3 hour marks). 5 hour marks is wider.

Answer: greater than a right angle

Counting angles in a shape

Count the corners. Every corner of a shape with straight sides is an angle, also a corner that points inwards.

Example

Priya cuts one corner off a rectangle with one straight cut. How many angles does the new shape have?

The cut takes away 1 corner and makes 2 new corners. 4 − 1 + 2 = 5.

Answer: 5 angles

Turns and clock hands

When a clock hand turns, it makes an angle. A quarter turn makes a right angle. A half turn is 2 right angles and a full turn is 4 right angles.

Example

The minute hand makes a quarter turn. How many minutes is that?

A full turn is 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15.

Answer: 15 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleLook at how wide the arms open, not how long they are
Saying a turned square corner is not a right angleTurn the page or use a checker: turning does not change an angle
Not counting a corner that points inwardsCount every corner of the shape
Calling curved lines an angleThe arms of an angle are straight lines

faq.q: What do P3 students learn about angles?
faq.a: They learn that an angle is made by two straight arms meeting at a vertex, find right angles in shapes and objects, and say if an angle is greater or smaller than a right angle. This is part of Geometry in the MOE Primary 3 syllabus.

faq.q: How do I explain a right angle to my child?
faq.a: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book or a door. Fold a piece of paper in half and in half again to make a right-angle checker, then look for square corners at home.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with angles in P3?
faq.a: Thinking that longer arms make a bigger angle. The size of an angle is how wide the arms open. Another mistake is saying a turned square corner is not a right angle.

faq.q: Do Primary 3 students measure angles in degrees?
faq.a: No. In P3 students compare angles with a right angle. Measuring angles in degrees with a protractor comes in Primary 4.

sets.title: What is an angle? Arms and vertex

items.q: Which point is the vertex of the angle?
items.e: A is where the two arms meet, so A is the vertex. The other points are on the arms.

items.q: Which of these has an angle?
items.e: At the corner of a table, two straight edges meet at a point. Round things have no angles.

items.q: Which angle is bigger?
items.e: Angle Q opens wider. Angle P has longer arms, but that does not make it bigger.

items.q: Which picture does not show an angle?
items.e: Picture C has curved lines. The arms of an angle must be straight lines, so C is not an angle.

items.q: How many vertices does one angle have?
items.e: The 2 arms meet at just 1 point. So one angle has 1 vertex.

items.q: Which point is the vertex of the angle?
items.e: C is where the two arms meet, so C is the vertex. The other points are on the arms.

items.q: Devi says the arms of an angle must be straight lines. Ryan says the arms can be curved. Who is right?
items.e: An angle is made by two straight lines that meet at a point. Curved lines do not make an angle.

items.q: Which picture shows an angle?
items.e: Picture A has two straight arms that meet at a point. The others are curved lines, two lines that do not meet, or just one line.

items.q: Which angle is bigger?
items.e: Both angles open the same amount. Angle P only has longer arms. Arm length does not change the size of an angle.

items.q: Which point is the vertex of the angle?
items.e: B is where the two arms meet, so B is the vertex. The other points are on the arms.

items.q: The two hands of this clock make an angle. Where is the vertex?
c: at the centre of the clock
at the tip of the long hand
items.e: The hands are the arms. They meet at the centre of the clock, so the vertex is at the centre.

items.q: An angle is made when two straight lines meet at what?
items.e: Two straight lines that meet at a point make an angle. The point is the vertex.

items.q: Sarah opens her laptop. Where is the vertex of the angle between the screen and the keyboard?
c: at the top of the screen
at the front of the keyboard
items.e: The screen and the keyboard are the arms. They meet at the hinge, so the vertex is at the hinge.

items.q: What are the two straight lines of an angle called?
items.e: An angle has two arms. They meet at the vertex.
L, V and N are made of straight lines that meet, so they have angles. O is a curve. It has no angles.

items.q: How many arms does an angle have?
items.e: An angle is made by 2 straight lines, so it has 2 arms.

items.q: Hui Min opens a pair of scissors wider. What happens to the angle between the blades?
items.e: The blades are like two arms. When they open wider, the angle gets bigger.

items.q: Which point is the vertex of the angle?
items.e: D is where the two arms meet, so D is the vertex. The other points are on the arms.

items.q: Wei Ming draws an angle. Then he makes both arms longer. He does not move them. What happens to the angle?
items.e: The size of an angle is how wide the arms open. Longer arms open the same amount, so the angle stays the same.

items.q: Two straight lines meet at a point to make an angle. What is that point called?
items.e: The point where the two lines meet is the vertex of the angle.

sets.title: Right angles in shapes and objects

items.q: Which object has no right angles?
items.e: Picture D is a give way sign. It is a triangle with 3 corners that are all smaller than a right angle. The others are rectangles.

items.q: How many right angles does this stop sign have?
items.e: A stop sign has 8 corners, but each one is greater than a right angle. So it has no right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: It is a rectangle that has been turned. It still has 4 square corners: 4 right angles.

items.q: Mei Ling says this is not a right angle because it is turned. Is she right?
c: No, it is still a right angle
Yes, it is greater than a right angle
Yes, right angles must stand up straight
Yes, it is smaller than a right angle
items.e: Turn the page and the arms make a square corner. Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: Which object has a right angle at every corner?
items.e: Picture B is a door. It is a rectangle, so all 4 corners are right angles. The pizza slice, coat hanger and give way sign have pointy or wide corners.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: All 3 corners are smaller than a right angle, so there are no right angles.

items.q: What does the small square in the corner show?
items.e: A small square in a corner shows a right angle: a square corner, like the corner of a page.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 corners on the left are right angles. The 2 corners on the right are not.

items.q: Ahmad says the tip of this slice of pizza is a right angle. Is he right?
c: Yes, it is a right angle
No, it is smaller than a right angle
No, it is greater than a right angle
items.e: The tip is much narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle is a right angle?
items.e: Picture D makes a square corner. It is turned and its arms are short, but it is still a right angle. Check with a right-angle checker.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: Only the bottom-left corner is a square corner. The other 2 corners are smaller.

items.q: Where can you find a right angle in the classroom?
c: the edge of a round clock
the tip of a sharp pencil
items.e: The corner of a whiteboard is a square corner: a right angle. A pencil tip is smaller than a right angle, and round things have no corners.

items.q: Raju checks the corners of his library book with a right-angle checker. How many corners are right angles?
items.e: The front cover is a rectangle. All 4 corners are square corners, so all 4 are right angles.

items.q: Priya folds a piece of paper in half, then in half again. What does the folded corner make?
c: an angle smaller than a right angle
an angle greater than a right angle
items.e: The first fold makes a straight edge. Folding that edge in half makes a square corner: a right angle. This is a right-angle checker.

items.q: This window of an HDB flat has 4 panes of glass. How many right angles does one pane have?
items.e: Each pane is a rectangle, so it has 4 square corners: 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: 5 corners are square corners. The corner that points inwards is greater than a right angle, so do not count it.

items.q: Which shape has no right angles?
items.e: Picture A leans over, so none of its corners are square corners. The turned square, the triangle and the L-shape all have right angles.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 right angle?
items.e: Picture C is a turned triangle with one square corner. The rectangle has 4 right angles, the other triangle has none and the 4-sided shape has 2.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 bottom corners and the top of the roof are right angles. The 2 corners where the roof meets the walls are greater.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: A square has 4 right angles. It is turned, but turning does not change the angles.

sets.title: Greater or smaller than a right angle

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Xin Yi says this angle is greater than a right angle because its arms are long. Is she right?
c: Yes, long arms make a big angle
No, it is a right angle
No, it is smaller than a right angle
items.e: Long arms do not make an angle bigger. This angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle in this triangle is greater than a right angle?
items.e: Angle B, at the top, opens wider than a square corner. Angles A and C are narrow: smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle is greater than a right angle?
items.e: Picture B opens wider than a square corner. Its arms are short, but that does not make it small.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle is smaller than a right angle?
items.e: Picture C is narrower than a square corner. The others are a right angle or wider.

items.q: Which angle in this shape is smaller than a right angle?
items.e: Angle B is narrower than a square corner. Angles A and D are right angles, and angle C is wider.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Ethan puts his right-angle checker into an angle. The angle is wider than the checker. What is the angle?
items.e: The checker is a right angle. If the angle is wider than the checker, it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Ali puts his right-angle checker into an angle. The checker does not fit: the angle is narrower. What is the angle?
items.e: The checker is a right angle. If the angle is narrower than the checker, it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The arms make a square corner, so it is a right angle. Turning an angle does not change it.

items.q: Nurul says this angle is smaller than a right angle because its arms are short. Is she right?
c: No, it is greater than a right angle
Yes, short arms make a small angle
No, it is a right angle
items.e: The size of an angle is how wide the arms open, not how long they are. This angle opens wider than a right angle.

items.q: Put the angles in order from the smallest to the greatest.
items.e: Y is smaller than a right angle, Z is a right angle and X is greater than a right angle. Look at how wide the arms open, not the arm length.

items.q: Arjun puts his right-angle checker into a corner of the canteen table. It fits exactly. What is the corner?
items.e: The checker is a right angle. If it fits exactly, with no gap, the corner is a right angle too.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle in this shape is greater than a right angle?
items.e: Angle C opens wider than a square corner. Angles A and D are right angles, and angle B is narrower.

items.q: Compare this angle with a right angle. What is it?
items.e: The arms make a square corner, so it is a right angle. Turning an angle does not change it.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Every triangle has 3 corners, so it has 3 angles, even when one angle is wide.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Count the corners: there are 6. So the shape has 6 angles.

items.q: How many angles in this shape are smaller than a right angle?
items.e: The 2 sharp corners are smaller than a right angle. The 2 wide corners are greater.

items.q: How many angles in this shape are greater than a right angle?
items.e: The 2 corners where the roof meets the walls are wider than a square corner. The other 3 are right angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: A circle has no straight lines and no corners, so it has no angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Cutting off a corner turns 1 corner into 2 corners. 3 + 2 = 5 angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Count every corner, also the 2 that point inwards under the top. There are 8 corners, so 8 angles.

items.q: How many angles are there in the capital letter F?
items.e: F has 1 angle at the top corner and 2 angles where the middle line meets the upright line: 3 angles.

items.q: How many angles are there in the capital letter N?
items.e: N has 1 angle at the top-left and 1 angle at the bottom-right, where the lines meet: 2 angles.

items.q: Jun Jie cuts one corner off a square piece of paper with one straight cut. How many angles does the new shape have?
items.e: The cut takes away 1 corner but makes 2 new corners. 4 − 1 + 2 = 5 angles.

items.q: How many angles are there in the capital letter X?
items.e: The two lines of X cross. They make 4 angles around the middle point.

items.q: Which shape has 5 angles?
items.e: Picture A has 5 corners, so it has 5 angles. The rectangle has 4, the triangle has 3 and the last shape has 6.

items.q: How many angles in this shape are smaller than a right angle?
items.e: Only the corner at the bottom right is narrower than a square corner. The 2 left corners are right angles and the top right corner is wide.

items.q: How many angles are there in the capital letter T?
items.e: The top line meets the stem in the middle. There is 1 angle on each side: 2 angles.

items.q: How many angles are there in the capital letter E?
items.e: E has 1 angle at the top corner, 2 angles where the middle line meets the upright line and 1 at the bottom corner: 4 angles.

items.q: A closed shape has 7 straight sides. How many angles does it have?
items.e: A shape with straight sides has as many angles as sides. 7 sides, so 7 angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Count every corner, also the one that points inwards. There are 6 corners, so 6 angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: A triangle has 3 corners, so it has 3 angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: Count the corners: there are 5. So the shape has 5 angles.

items.q: How many angles does this shape have?
items.e: A square has 4 corners, so it has 4 angles. Turning the square does not change this.

items.q: A capsule on the Singapore Flyer goes all the way round once. It comes back to where it started. What turn has it made?
items.e: Going all the way round and back to the start is a full turn.

items.q: Siti opens her laptop so that the screen leans back a little past a square corner. What angle do the screen and keyboard make?
items.e: A square corner is a right angle. The screen opens a little wider than that, so the angle is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Kumar walks along the void deck. At the lift lobby, he turns right. What turn does he make?
items.e: Turning right makes a square corner with the way you were walking. That is a quarter turn.
From 6 round to 3 is 6 to 9, 9 to 12 and 12 to 3: 3 quarter turns. That is a three-quarter turn.
The hand goes all the way round from 9 back to 9: a full turn.

items.q: What do the hands of the clock make at 6 o’clock?
c: an angle smaller than a right angle
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point in opposite directions. Together they make a straight line: a half turn.

items.q: How many minutes does the minute hand take to make a quarter turn?
items.e: A full turn of the minute hand takes 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15, so a quarter turn takes 15 minutes.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a right angle?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the long hand points to 12 and the short hand points to 3. They make a square corner.

items.q: Chloe turns the tap on with a half turn. How many right angles has the handle turned through?
items.e: A half turn is 2 quarter turns, and each quarter turn is a right angle. So the handle turns through 2 right angles.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 1 o’clock the hands are only 1 hour mark apart. That is narrower than a right angle (3 hour marks).

items.q: From 12 noon to 6 pm, what turn does the hour hand make?
items.e: The hour hand moves from 12 to 6. That is halfway round the clock: a half turn.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from the dashed line to where it is now. What turn has it made?
items.e: From 3 to 9 is halfway round the clock: a half turn.

items.q: From 12 noon to 3 pm, what turn does the hour hand make?
items.e: The hour hand moves from 12 to 3. That is a quarter of the way round the clock: a quarter turn.

items.q: Farah opens the classroom door until it makes a square corner with the wall. What turn has the door made?
items.e: A square corner is a right angle, and a right angle is a quarter turn.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands make a square corner: a right angle.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from the dashed line to where it is now. What turn has it made?
items.e: From 12 to 3 is a quarter of the way round the clock: a quarter turn.

items.q: Recess starts at 9.45 am. When it ends, the minute hand has made a half turn. What time does recess end?
items.e: A half turn of the minute hand is 30 minutes. 30 minutes after 9.45 am is 10.15 am.

items.q: On Sports Day, Hafiz faces the finishing line. He makes a half turn. Which way does he face now?
items.e: A half turn is 2 right angles. It makes you face the opposite way, away from the finishing line.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 hour marks apart. A right angle is only 3 hour marks, so this angle is greater.

items.q: School ends at 1.30 pm. While Kavya packs her bag, the minute hand makes a quarter turn. What time is it now?
items.e: A quarter turn of the minute hand is 15 minutes. 15 minutes after 1.30 pm is 1.45 pm.
